gettingStarted.title: 0. Getting Started
gettingStarted.prerequisite: An Ubuntu computer or WSL2 console, sudo access and a tested public release. For a public server, also prepare your domain and DNS.
gettingStarted.outcome: You know which installation path to follow and how configuration, service data and recovery fit together.
gettingStarted.markdown:
## Your first platform, step by step

The **Bootstrapper** runs your platform. The **Wizard** configures it in your browser. **Sync** connects the two. You do not need Kubernetes experience.

1. [Quick Install](#docs/quickstart) on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 / 26.04 LTS x86_64 host with sudo, curl, internet, at least 8 GiB RAM and 40 GiB free disk. Or choose [manual Ubuntu/WSL2 installation](#docs/installation) or the public-server HTTPS path.
2. [Connect and configure](#docs/configuration). Open **Wizard**, choose the pencil beside **Connect**, enter your own Sync address and credentials, then **Submit → Synchronize → Fetch**.
3. Review the settings, keep a private **Backup**, then **Push**. Push applies the configuration and restarts services automatically.
4. [Set up a runner](#docs/runners), then [create your first project](#docs/projects). Wait for its build and deployment jobs before opening its domain.

> **Tip:** Start with local HTTP to learn the workflow. Use the full public-server guide before exposing services to the internet.

## Keep two kinds of backup

**Open / Backup** and **Fetch / Push** manage configuration, including secrets. **Harvest / Seed** protects persistent service data. A configuration ZIP does not contain GitLab databases or repositories. See [Recovery](#docs/recovery) before relying on a backup.

## Check your starting point

Run this in your Ubuntu console:

```bash
uname -m
git --version
```

The public release targets `x86_64` / `linux/amd64`. Quick Install downloads the tested release and starts the initial Wizard; follow its protected first-access instructions, then continue in your browser. Downloads and initialization take time. The manual installation chapter covers Git, Docker, release inputs and checks. Existing installations and Seed recovery use their separate documented paths.

> **Info:** Example domains and release placeholders belong to your own deployment. A standalone Wizard does not start Sync, GitLab or runners.

foundations.title: 2. Foundations
foundations.prerequisite: Read Getting Started and choose an installation path.
foundations.outcome: You understand the services, state boundaries and the order of everyday configuration tasks.
foundations.markdown:
## The pieces of your platform

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Bootstrapper | Starts and coordinates containers and persistent storage |
| Wizard | Browser interface for configuration, runners and projects |
| Sync | Authenticated API between the Wizard and the Bootstrapper |
| GitLab | Source repositories, merge requests and pipelines |
| Runner managers | Execute pipeline jobs in a shared runner pool |
| Registry | Stores the container images built by pipelines |
| NGINX | Routes each configured domain to its service or environment |

## A safe configuration cycle

**Connect → Fetch → edit → Backup → Push → reconnect → Fetch.** Fetch loads saved settings, or marked suggestions on first setup. Review suggestions before transfer. Push applies settings and restarts services automatically.

> **Warning:** Backup files contain credentials. Keep them private. Configuration backups and completed service-data Seeds are separate recovery inputs.

## What survives a change

Source and images describe the infrastructure. Persistent service data contains repositories, databases, registry content and secrets. Saved configuration takes precedence over first-install examples. [Working storage](#docs/storage) explains local data, optional live volumes and independent backup media.

## Build, verify, promote

A source import installs source. A build produces a candidate. Review and Beta are optional environments. Production promotion is a separate deliberate operation with exact image evidence and a rollback checkpoint. Follow [Evolution](#docs/evolution) for the full platform and the linked Wizard guides for interface delivery.

development-previews: Healthy GitLab, registry and runners; selected source projects, exact preview DNS names and certificates.
Explicit setup creates verified preview bindings while the accepted Production image remains selected.
coordinated-backup: A configured platform and the selected mounted external backup medium with sufficient free space.
A native Harvest and matching configuration ZIP form two independently retained recovery inputs.
host-operations: Access to the Linux x86_64 Docker daemon host and the selected immutable workload images.
You distinguish CPU, upstream-kernel and image failures and verify bounded logs with preserved settings.
token-expiry: An authenticated Sync connection and explicit automation project paths in saved configuration.
Known expiry dates and honest unknown states guide renewal without exposing or rotating credentials.
system-diagnostics: An authenticated Sync connection and configured registry, helper image and managed runner pool.
Bounded server checks and an optional explicit Docker pull distinguish connectivity from authentication and image availability.
guided-preview-acceptance: A retained installation identity, matching native controller/source, TLS hosts and runner prerequisites are available.

Native shared Beta setup/binding, HTTPS deploy/stop and unchanged Production are verified; pipeline authorization uses an explicit contract verifier, without native MR/default-branch pipelines or System Review.
dependency-security: The declared Node/npm toolchains, committed lockfiles and the affected application/build checks.
You can audit actual dependency paths, apply stable compatible fixes and validate scoped overrides without bypassing release gates.
dependency-updates: Protected source branches, reviewed Renovate configuration and private operator provisioning inputs.
Scheduled discovery proposes grouped stable updates only after explicit dashboard approval; existing merge and deployment gates remain.
quickstart: A fresh Ubuntu 24.04 / 26.04 LTS x86_64 host with sudo, curl, internet, 8 GiB RAM and 40 GiB free disk.
One maintained command starts the initial Wizard; you continue platform setup in the browser.
releases: Public release access and the source/image identities of the version you want to install.
You can inspect versioned public metadata, release notes and the accepted publication boundary.
architecture: Read Getting Started for the platform’s practical installation and configuration workflow.
You understand the 2019 origin, source-as-DNA principle, generation model and future vision.
system-review: An accepted candidate, an explicitly reserved Beta HTTPS host and the required System checks.
You can inspect and stop the exact bundled Wizard candidate before deliberate Production promotion.
host-preparation: Ubuntu with sudo, Docker access, selected working storage and trusted release source/image identities.
The selected release starts with the intended images, storage mode and host integration.
aliases: A configured canonical Wizard hostname, DNS for every alias and certificates covering HTTPS aliases.
Alias requests redirect to the canonical Wizard while preserving paths, queries and certificate challenges.
project-guide: Connect and Fetch; select a GitLab namespace, unique lowercase/digit Project Key, template and environment domains.
The private repository and managed pipeline are created; successful jobs deploy each automatic environment.
project-contract: A configured GitLab instance and Sync connection; choose a new unoccupied repository identity.
You understand template provisioning, retry behavior, ownership and the separate Wizard workflow.
runner-persistence: Selected persistent working storage and a configured runner pool. Fetch before changing its scale or token.
Runner managers retain their individual identities across container recreation and scale changes.
storage: Choose local working data or an explicitly mounted live volume, and a separate backup target when needed.
Live paths, storage guards, certificate state and independent Seed media match your selected layout.
seed-recovery: A completed verified Seed, matching private configuration, compatible GitLab image and fresh live storage.
Service data is restored before writers start, then authenticated runtime and retained data are verified.
git-mirror: Choose the canonical GitLab project, resolve source history and prepare an existing optional GitHub mirror plus private credentials.
Reviewed merged code is mirrored while GitLab state and service-data recovery retain their separate contracts.
wizard-source: Matching System/Wizard versions, an owned managed Wizard scaffold and the prepared pinned source package.
The exact source is explicitly imported without starting a pipeline or replacing the running interface.
wizard-build: Imported Wizard source, matching controller recipe, registry and a trusted runner with sufficient build resources.
Required build/browser evidence verifies an immutable candidate image without promoting Production.
wizard-environments: A verified candidate, reserved Review/Beta hosts, matching certificates and an explicitly provisioned helper.
Manual candidate environments can be deployed and removed without replacing the Production Wizard.
wizard-production: Exact accepted candidate evidence, explicit promotion authority and a retained previous immutable image/checkpoint.
A reviewed plan switches the Wizard deliberately and preserves an inspectable rollback path.
wizard-upgrade: An owned managed project, accepted upgrade source, current repository head and a reserved CI slot.
The reviewed migration preserves user changes and upgrades source or managed recipes through an ordinary merge request.
wizard-source-primary: An existing private Wizard source project, registry, native checks and retained ownership/recovery inputs.
One adopted repository supplies source, reviews, builds and immutable delivery evidence.
wizard-build-reference: A supported imported Wizard source revision, matching managed recipe and trusted Docker build/browser runner.
The recipe's activation, required gates, toolchain and trust-store contracts can be verified.
controller-reference: A clean accepted checkout, exact source/image identities, chosen persistence selector and the operation's private inputs.
You can select the documented controller install, initialization, promotion or recovery-export operation and verify its receipts.
verification: An accepted checkout with exact submodules, Docker and the capacity/isolation required by the selected check.
The applicable component or platform checks produce reproducible evidence with explicit live-test boundaries.
candidate-testing: Trusted candidate code, an explicit capacity lease, isolated disposable state and required fixture/image inputs.
The candidate is checked against declared startup, migration and recovery boundaries, with owned cleanup recorded.
